newsitem.title: CHINA: Wife of jailed Chinese dissident sues government.
newsitem.headline: Wife of jailed Chinese dissident sues government.

text.p: The wife of a jailed Chinese dissident said on Friday she has filed a lawsuit against authorities in Shanghai for refusing to let her visit or exchange correspondence with her husband.
Zhu Yaping, wife of Yao Zhenxiang, said she pressed charges before the Shanghai Intermediate People's Court on July 29, accusing local authorities of infringing upon her rights.
"I haven't received a single letter from my husband since April. This is against the law," Zhu said in a telephone interview. "I haven't met my husband since he was arrested."
Yao, 37, fled to Hong Kong in 1994 and was granted political asylum in France. He returned to Shanghai in February 1996 after police promised not to arrest him.
Despite the promise, Yao and his brother were arrested in April last year, and accused of illegally leaving China and distributing pornographic material.
Yao was ordered to serve three years of "re-education through labour" at a labour camp in the eastern coastal province of Jiangsu.

"Re-education through labour" is an administrative punishment that can be imposed without a trial, and Western diplomats say Chinese officials increasingly favour it as a way of removing political dissidents from circulation without a complicated judicial process.
Officials could not be reached for comment.
Beijing rejects criticisms of its policies on dissent as interference in its internal affairs, arguing that the right to the bare necessities of life is more than important than political rights.
